==Summary==
The Scots Gard’ner [in two parts…]. Together with The Gardiner’s Kalendar by John Reid. Edited by Alfred H. Hyatt. With an appreciation by the Earl of Rosebery.
Author
Hyatt, Alfred H. (Editor); Reid, John
Title
The Scots Gard’ner [in two parts…]. Together with The Gardiner’s Kalendar by John Reid. Edited by Alfred H. Hyatt. With an appreciation by the Earl of Rosebery.
Object type book binding
Date 1907
date QS:P571,+1907-00-00T00:00:00Z/9
Dimensions 127 × 160 × 25 mm (5 × 6.29 × 0.98 in)
Collection British Library
Accession number
C188a750
Place of creation London & Edinburgh: T. N. Foulis, 1907 196p. Edinburgh: Printed by Neill and Company Limited.
Notes Robin de Beaumont’s small square bookplate is on the upper endpaper verso. He has noted: [Book purchased:] ‘18 October 1969 4.0’. This work is number IV in “The Garden Lover’s Series”. Decorated endpapers and pastedowns, showing a landscape with a sundial. Green cloth. No blocking on the lower cover. The upper cover shows a garden path, leading up to a castle. (possibly after Ethel Hargreaves?) At the head, the lettering in gilt is: “/ The Scots Gard’ner/ [at the tail in black] John Reid/”. The spine has gilt lettering at the head: “/ The/ Scots/ Gard’ner/”. Beneath this is a tree and “/ John Reid/” blocked in black, with “Foulis” in black at the tail. This book acquired with the generous assistance of the British Library Collections Trust. Another copy (probably) of this work is at British Library shelf mark 12274de
References

The Library of the late Robin de Beaumont. Bonhams Auction Catalogue [online sale of 31 January 2024.] Lot 53. Ian Elfick and Paul Harris, T.N. Foulis. The History and Bibliography of an Edinburgh Publishing House, 1998, no. 161 TN Foulis https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._N._Foulis
